clue.text: You can't Adam and Eve it!

definitions.text: You can't Adam and Eve it!

parts.words: You can't Adam and Eve it!
parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang 'Adam and Eve' means believe, so this is something you cannot believe: an untruth, itself rhyming slang for a lie

explanation.walkthrough: Two layers of Cockney rhyming slang: 'Adam and Eve' = believe, and the answer (via 'pork pie') = lie, so a thing you can't believe is a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for a lie, which is exactly what a listener cannot believe.

clue.text: Architect seen to be right in new erection

indicators.note: the letter for right is set inside the rearranged letters, as if placed in the building
this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
an erection is something constructed, so the letters of new are built into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An architect is spotted standing beside a newly put-up building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erection' turns NEW into WEN; R goes inside after the W. Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren is England's most famous architect, designer of St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: College accommodates a large number here in Gloucestershire

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so one piece is lodged within the other

parts.note: Keble is a college of Oxford University
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A college finds room for a crowd of people at a Gloucestershire location.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloucestershire is an English county in the west; Kemble is a village there, with a railway station serving Cirencester.
explanation.definitionFit: Kemble is a village in the Cotswolds of Gloucestershire, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Spring flower Spooner calls unadorned misery

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version of the phrase swaps them

parts.note: unadorned means bare, without decoration
hell is extreme misery

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a famous verbal tic names a spring flower as utter wretchedness.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the B and H of 'bare hell' gives the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The harebell is a delicate blue wild flower of the bellflower family.

clue.text: Tories rise to be sprayed with spit

indicators.note: spraying scatters things about, so the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Conservatives stand up only to be showered with spittle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spit' looks like the spittle doing the spraying, but it is the definition: a roasting skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting spit is the turning rod of a rotating grill, the apparatus named by the answer.

clue.text: Something quite clear can easily become mysterious

indicators.note: only something of these words is wanted, a run of letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A thing that is perfectly plain can quickly turn baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside cle-AR CAN E-asily; 'quite' is just padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane knowledge is secret or understood by few, hence mysterious.

clue.text: Moderation, yet Boris might achieve it

indicators.note: the clue suggests the letters could, if reworked, reach this state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sly dig that even a famously boisterous politician might manage to stay sober.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris is Boris Johnson, the British politician known for exuberance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobriety means temperance, a moderate restraint especially in drinking.

clue.text: Shout with painful cry and colour

parts.note: to yell is to shout
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone shouts, yelps in pain and goes a different shade.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a primary colour, that of lemons and buttercups.

clue.text: Maybe a group of bankers all at sea?

definitions.meaning: a board of directors, for example at a bank, is a governing group
on board ship, sailing on the sea

explanation.walkthrough: Read as A BOARD it is a bank's board; as one word it means on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an executive committee such as a bank's directors; the other is being on a vessel.

clue.text: It's like baking without gas

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: BG is short for British Gas, the UK energy supplier

explanation.surface: Cooking with no oven fuel is much the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B and G from BAKING; British Gas is a well-known British energy company.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means similar or related, the same as alike.

clue.text: Boy hugs girl in Essex

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping arms around, so one name encloses the other

parts.note: Billy is a boy's name
Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young couple embrace somewhere in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county east of London; Billericay is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Billericay is a market town in the English county of Essex.

clue.text: Wed without children? Nits!

parts.note: s.p. stands for sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in genealogies
nits are the eggs of lice, standing here for lice

explanation.surface: A dismissive reaction to someone marrying without having kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nits!' reads as an exclamation of scorn, but it supplies the lice.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting spliced is informal slang for getting married.

clue.text: Tories' rule broken, lacking purpose …

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Conservative government has collapsed and the country drifts aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Irresolute describes someone indecisive, without firm purpose.

clue.text: How Rees becomes the foreman?

parts.note: the prophet's word seer turned over spells the name Rees

explanation.surface: A man named Rees gets promoted to supervisor.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split the answer as OVER + SEER, an instruction to turn SEER over, which gives REES; 'becomes' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer supervises workers, which is the job of a foreman.

clue.text: Hide endless Mediterranean island

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: the Mediterranean is a sea
Crete is a Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean island without limits serves as a hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it.

clue.text: … thanks to fast party leader with ability

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party when this was set

explanation.surface: Gratitude to a quick-witted political chief for his skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but is the Lenten fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Talented means gifted, possessing skill or ability.

clue.text: With apprehension of little boys at arm's length

indicators.note: the boys stand at the arm's two ends, keeping it between them, so the arm sits inside

parts.note: Al is a short form of a boy's name such as Alan
Ed is a short form of a boy's name such as Edward
the arm itself, flanked by the two short names

explanation.surface: Someone nervously keeps small children at arm's length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'length' just completes the phrase arm's length: the boys hold the arm between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed means frightened or anxious, full of apprehension.

clue.text: Military order (excluding front rank) that makes sense

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: eyes right is a parade-ground command

indicators.note: front means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drill command, missing its front line, still somehow makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop R (front of 'rank') from EYES RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses.

clue.text: It helps to do them wrong

indicators.note: doing something wrong garbles it, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A guide to getting things right by first getting them wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a procedure that helps get a task done.

clue.text: Break up with plunge over reflected failure

indicators.note: the plunge is placed over the other piece, covering it on both sides

parts.note: to dive is to plunge

indicators.note: a reflection is reversed, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a loss is a failure

explanation.surface: A relationship ends in a plunge after a failure looked back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' means the plunge is laid over the other piece, wrapping round it; 'reflected' means that failure word is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve a partnership or parliament is to break it up.

clue.text: One grows up and blooms

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
rises means goes up

explanation.surface: A plant sprouts and flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are flowers, so they are blooms.

clue.text: Well this is a bit rich!

definitions.text: Well this is a bit rich!

parts.words: Well this is a bit rich!
parts.note: add the word well before this and the phrase means rich, and this is part of that rich phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation of outrage hides 'well-heeled', meaning wealthy: this word is the bit after 'well'.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled means prosperous, so this word is the second part of a term for rich.

clue.text: Where one lives without a good reverence for one's superior?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: home is where one lives

explanation.surface: A question about whether a home without decent respect suits a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: HOME goes round A + G.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is respect paid, originally by a vassal to his lord.

clue.text: Where to get off colour in cloth

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: gingham is a checked cotton cloth
off colour means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: Advice on where to buy faded fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Gillingham is a town in Kent (and one in Dorset), so the bare 'Where' defines a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Kent, so it answers the question of a place.

clue.text: Ineffectual character died with a short prayer

parts.note: RIP abbreviates requiescat in pace, a prayer for the dead

explanation.surface: A weakling dies with a brief prayer said over him.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is slang for a feeble, dull person.

clue.text: Something raised short of a bloomer

indicators.note: short of means the final letter is missing

parts.note: a daisy is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A raised object that falls short of being a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake (British slang) but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform in a hall.

clue.text: Insect let out another

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One insect releases a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: another insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is another kind of insect, following the bee in the clue.

clue.text: Encounter that's not just pettish?

parts.note: a scrap between dogs is literally pets fighting, but the phrase means an aerial or close-quarters battle

explanation.walkthrough: Pets fighting suggests a scrap between dogs, yet the term means aerial combat between fighter planes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogfight is a close air battle between fighter aircraft, a fierce encounter.
